evidence.title: Effects of dietary fat on fertility of dairy cattle: A meta-analysis and meta-regression.
evidence.abstract: Evidence is increasing of positive effects of feeding fats during transition on fertility and the adaptation to lactation. This study used meta-analytic methods to explore the effects of including fats in the transition diet on the risk of pregnancy to service (proportion pregnant) and calving to pregnancy interval. Meta-analysis was used to integrate smaller studies and increase the statistical power over that of any single study and explore new hypotheses. We explored the effect of fats and diet composition on fertility using meta-regression methods. Relatively few highly controlled studies are available providing detailed descriptions of the diets used that examined interactions between fat nutrition and reproductive outcomes. Only 17 studies containing 26 comparisons were suitable for inclusion in statistical evaluations. Reproductive variables evaluated were risk of pregnancy (proportion pregnant), primarily to first service, and calving to pregnancy interval. Production variables examined were milk yield, milk composition, and body weight. The sources of heterogeneity in these studies were also explored. A 27% overall increase in pregnancy to service was observed (relative risk=1.27; 95% confidence interval Knapp Hartung 1.09 to 1.45), and results were relatively consistent (I(2)=19.9%). A strong indication of a reduction in calving to pregnancy interval was also identified, which was consistent across studies (I(2)=0.0%), supporting a conclusion that, overall, the inclusion of fats does improve fertility. Further exploration of the factors contributing to proportion pregnant using bivariate meta-regression identified variables that reflected changes in diet composition or animal response resulting from inclusion of the fat interventions in the experimental diets fed. Increased fermentable neutral detergent fiber and soluble fiber intakes increased the proportion pregnant, whereas increased milk yield of the treatment group decreased this measure. Unexpectedly, the estimated energy costs of urea production also had a positive association with proportion pregnant. The limited number of suitable studies for the analysis highlights the need for more work to improve understanding of the critical nutritional factors affecting fertility. These factors include specific fatty acids in dietary interventions that contribute to increasing fertility of cows in dai

evidence.title: The role of beta-carotene in cattle infertility, mastitis and milk yield: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
evidence.abstract: The impact of beta-carotene on cattle fertility has been investigated in various studies; however, consensus on this issue has not been reached. In the present study, we systematically reviewed and meta-analysed 29 publications conducted between 1984 and 2022, focusing on seven fertility measures, clinical mastitis and milk yield in cows. We did not find statistically significant results in 8 out of 11 parameters (p > .05). Statistically significant results were observed for milk yield (MD: 216.25 kg in 305 days, p = .01, CI: 50.73-381.77), pregnancy at first service (OR: 1.38 CI: 1.08-1.76, p = .01) and clinical mastitis (OR: 0.59, CI: 0.44-0.80, p = .006) in favour of beta-carotene supplementation. The meta-regression revealed significant effects of 'plasma beta-carotene levels' on 'service to per pregnancy' and dose on 'milk yield' (p = .04 and p = 0). In binary outcomes, 'dose × day' and 'plasma beta-carotene concentration in the control group' positively influenced pregnancy at first service (p = .02 and .03). In conclusion, given the positive point direction observed for some variables and insignificant results for others, there is a need for more studies. We note the very high heterogeneity of outcomes and suggest caution in interpreting results.

evidence.title: Automated feature extraction and selection for data-driven models of rapid battery capacity fade and end of life
evidence.abstract: Lithium-ion cells may experience rapid degradation in later life, especially with more extreme usage protocols. The onset of rapid degradation is called the `knee point', and forecasting it is important for the safe and economically viable use for batteries. We propose a data-driven method that uses automated feature selection to produce inputs for a Gaussian process regression model that estimates changes in battery health, from which the entire capacity fade trajectory, knee point and end of life may be predicted. The feature selection procedure flexibly adapts to varying inputs and prioritises those that impact degradation. For the datasets considered, it was found that calendar time and time spent in specific voltage regions had a strong impact on degradation rate. The approach produced median root mean square errors on capacity estimates under 1\%, and also produced median knee point and end of life prediction errors of 2.6\% and 1.3\% respectively.

evidence.title: An Acausal Li-Ion Battery Pack Model for  Automotive Applications
evidence.abstract: In this work, a novel acausal and reconfigurable battery pack model is presented. The model structure adopted for the battery cell is based on an equivalent circuit representation. The circuit elements are modified to take account of both hysteresis and diffusion limitation. The latter is known to be a nonlinear function of large operating currents or long operating times. It is shown that the integration of a current dependent time constant within the cell model better emulates the solid diffusional dynamics of lithium intercalation into the active material under large electrical loads. The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified. The cell and scaled-up pack model are parameterized for a number of commercially available cell formats, energy capacities and chemistries. The new models are validated using transient, real-world, electrical data measured from an electric vehicle (EV) operating within an urban environment

variation and the impact this can have on the design of highly

evidence.title: Characterising Li-ion battery degradation through the identification of perturbations in electrochemical battery models
evidence.abstract: Lithium ion batteries undergo complex electrochemical and mechanical degradation. This complexity is pronounced in applications such as electric vehicles where highly demanding cycles of operation and varying environmental conditions lead to non-trivial interactions of ageing stress factors. This work presents the framework for an ageing diagnostic tool based on identifying the physical parameters of a fundamental electrochemistry-based battery model from non-invasive voltage/current cycling tests. Exploiting the embedded symbolic manipulation tool and global optimiser in MapleSim, computational cost is reduced, significantly facilitating rapid optimisation. The diagnostic tool is used to study the degradation of a 3Ah LiC6/LiNiCoAlO2 battery stored at 45°C at 50% State of Charge for 202 days; the results agree with expected battery degradation

mechanism_map.mechanism: Pooling many small units into one integrated aggregate produces greater power/capacity than any single unit can deliver alone, and smooths unit-level heterogeneity (weakest-unit limitations).
mechanism_map.intervention: Rebuild the drill battery pack as a modular multi-bank array: several smaller cell modules wired in parallel with an active balancing controller and current-sharing bus, so heavy-load current is split across all modules instead of stressing one string; add a supercapacitor buffer at the output port to absorb transition surges at load onset.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: Sustained heavy-load output through a full shift with markedly lower per-cell current and heat, because aggregate capacity is pooled across modules and no single cell carries the full load, slowing capacity fade.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Run the multi-bank pack and a baseline single-string pack of equal nominal capacity on identical heavy-load drilling duty cycles; log per-cell current, temperature, and capacity retention over a full shift and 500 cycles. Hypothesis is falsified if the multi-bank pack shows no measurable reduction in per-cell stress/temperature and no slower fade, or if balancing leaves cells outside a set tolerance (e.g., >50 mV divergence).
mechanism_map.mechanism_source_span: Meta-analysis was used to integrate smaller studies and increase the statistical power over that of any single study

It is shown that the integration of a current dependent time constant within the cell model better emulates the solid diffusional dynamics of lithium intercalation into the active material under large electrical loads. The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified. The cell and scaled-up pack model are parameterized for a number of commercially available cell formats, energy capacities and chemistries. The new models are validated using transient, real-world, electrical data measured from an electric vehicle (EV) operating within an urban environment

parallelized battery systems

candidates.mechanism: Capacity fade under heavy load is driven by per-cell current density and temperature: high current density raises overpotential, causing resistive (I²R) heating and lithium plating / SEI growth side reactions whose rates accelerate with temperature (Arrhenius); fade is therefore a function of the thermal-electrochemical stress per cell, not of pack-level nominal capacity. Paralleling N cell banks under an active balancing controller reduces current per bank toward 1/N of the load (governed by Kirchhoff's current law, with impedance-dependent sharing that the controller corrects), which lowers per-cell heating and side-reaction rate; this is a physical current-division effect, not an averaging or "pooling increases power" effect.
candidates.intervention: Rebuild the pack as a modular multi-bank array of N parallel cell modules, each with its own cell-level fuse, per-bank current-sense shunt, and a balancing controller that continuously trims per-bank current share to keep impedance-driven imbalance within tolerance; add a supercapacitor buffer at the output port to supply load-onset current spikes so the cells never see the transient peak. Thermal design ties per-bank temperature sensing to a current limit that throttles any bank exceeding a set cell temperature.
candidates.predicted_effect: Under identical heavy-load drilling duty cycles, per-bank current and cell temperature drop measurably versus a single-string pack of equal nominal capacity, and capacity retention over a full shift and 500 cycles improves by a quantified margin, because fade rate falls with reduced current density and cell temperature.
candidates.testable_prediction: Run the multi-bank pack and a baseline single-string pack of equal nominal capacity on identical heavy-load duty cycles, logging per-cell current, temperature, and discharge capacity over a full shift and 500 cycles; the hypothesis is killed if the multi-bank pack shows no reduction in per-cell current density/temperature, or no slower measured capacity fade, or if the balancing controller cannot hold cell currents within the set tolerance.
candidates.mechanism_source_span: Meta-analysis was used to integrate smaller studies and increase the statistical power over that of any single study
candidates.support_state_note: IMPROVE_CHILD_SUPPORT_NOT_ADJUDICATED: the child's mutated mechanism has no mechanism-space evidence adjudication; the release gate holds non-affirmative support states (R401 Phase 4)

kill_basis.verdict: KILLED - the record's own mechanism_source_span is verbatim text from a dairy-cattle fertility meta-analysis ("Meta-analysis was used to integrate smaller studies and increase the statistical power over that of any single study"), and the record maps that statistical-power-of-meta-analysis concept directly onto electrical/electrochemical power aggregation across battery modules; the specific element that fails to transfer is the equivalence between "statistical power gained by pooling study results" and "electrical power/current capacity gained by paralleling cells," since statistical pooling and electrical paralleling are physically different operations (averaging effect sizes vs. summing current delivery governed by Kirchhoff's current law and weakest-cell impedance), and the candidate's mechanism is explicitly grounded in this dairy paper's wording rather than any electrochemistry.

derivation_trace.causal_change: The parent's mechanism was an invalid transfer of "statistical power gained by pooling study results" (a dairy-cattle meta-analysis) onto electrical power aggregation; the child replaces that analogy with the actual physical cause chain — current density per cell → Joule heating and overpotential → temperature-accelerated side reactions (SEI growth / lithium plating) → capacity fade — so the claimed effect now follows from electrochemistry and Kirchhoff's current law rather than from meta-analysis wording.
derivation_trace.novel_design_variable: Per-cell current density and its induced thermal field as the fade-governing variable (with active per-bank current share and temperature-based throttling as the control input), instead of the parent's "aggregate pooled capacity / weakest-unit smoothing."

This RAISES the cross-domain bar (was the same >= 2 as same-domain) — stricter, not weaker (Art. VII).

warnings.mechanism: Capability collision test — keyword collision search is insufficient to establish novelty
warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.mechanism: RES-4 narrow: adaptive transverse/sigmoid sinus stent for CSF absorption regulation via AG pressure gradient control
informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.mechanism: Automated Sufficiency Proof Generator (CC-04 / MSES theorem) — formal proof that a specific evidence set E is sufficient to establish modification-specific clinical risk envelope R(Δ)
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. But deep collision revealed that each element (continuous renewal, dynamic topography, surface-energy modulation) is individually occupied by prior art. The combination is an aggregation of known anti-fouling approaches. The lesson: M4 must be assessed at the ELEMENT level, not the concept level. And M4=NOT FOUND means the search has not found comparable performance yet — not that it does not exist.

custody_records.raw_content: Evidence is increasing of positive effects of feeding fats during transition on fertility and the adaptation to lactation. This study used meta-analytic methods to explore the effects of including fats in the transition diet on the risk of pregnancy to service (proportion pregnant) and calving to pregnancy interval. Meta-analysis was used to integrate smaller studies and increase the statistical power over that of any single study and explore new hypotheses. We explored the effect of fats and diet composition on fertility using meta-regression methods. Relatively few highly controlled studies are available providing detailed descriptions of the diets used that examined interactions between fat nutrition and reproductive outcomes. Only 17 studies containing 26 comparisons were suitable for inclusion in statistical evaluations. Reproductive variables evaluated were risk of pregnancy (proportion pregnant), primarily to first service, and calving to pregnancy interval. Production variables examined were milk yield, milk composition, and body weight. The sources of heterogeneity in these studies were also explored. A 27% overall increase in pregnancy to service was observed (relative risk=1.27; 95% confidence interval Knapp Hartung 1.09 to 1.45), and results were relatively consistent (I(2)=19.9%). A strong indication of a reduction in calving to pregnancy interval was also identified, which was consistent across studies (I(2)=0.0%), supporting a conclusion that, overall, the inclusion of fats does improve fertility. Further exploration of the factors contributing to proportion pregnant using bivariate meta-regression identified variables that reflected changes in diet composition or animal response resulting from inclusion of the fat interventions in the experimental diets fed. Increased fermentable neutral detergent fiber and soluble fiber intakes increased the proportion pregnant, whereas increased milk yield of the treatment group decreased this measure. Unexpectedly, the estimated energy costs of urea production also had a positive association with proportion pregnant. The limited number of suitable studies for the analysis highlights the need for more work to improve understanding of the critical nutritional factors affecting fertility. These factors include specific fatty acids in dietary interventions that contribute to increasing fertility of cows in dai

custody_records.raw_content: The impact of beta-carotene on cattle fertility has been investigated in various studies; however, consensus on this issue has not been reached. In the present study, we systematically reviewed and meta-analysed 29 publications conducted between 1984 and 2022, focusing on seven fertility measures, clinical mastitis and milk yield in cows. We did not find statistically significant results in 8 out of 11 parameters (p > .05). Statistically significant results were observed for milk yield (MD: 216.25 kg in 305 days, p = .01, CI: 50.73-381.77), pregnancy at first service (OR: 1.38 CI: 1.08-1.76, p = .01) and clinical mastitis (OR: 0.59, CI: 0.44-0.80, p = .006) in favour of beta-carotene supplementation. The meta-regression revealed significant effects of 'plasma beta-carotene levels' on 'service to per pregnancy' and dose on 'milk yield' (p = .04 and p = 0). In binary outcomes, 'dose × day' and 'plasma beta-carotene concentration in the control group' positively influenced pregnancy at first service (p = .02 and .03). In conclusion, given the positive point direction observed for some variables and insignificant results for others, there is a need for more studies. We note the very high heterogeneity of outcomes and suggest caution in interpreting results.

custody_records.raw_content: Lithium-ion cells may experience rapid degradation in later life, especially with more extreme usage protocols. The onset of rapid degradation is called the `knee point', and forecasting it is important for the safe and economically viable use for batteries. We propose a data-driven method that uses automated feature selection to produce inputs for a Gaussian process regression model that estimates changes in battery health, from which the entire capacity fade trajectory, knee point and end of life may be predicted. The feature selection procedure flexibly adapts to varying inputs and prioritises those that impact degradation. For the datasets considered, it was found that calendar time and time spent in specific voltage regions had a strong impact on degradation rate. The approach produced median root mean square errors on capacity estimates under 1\%, and also produced median knee point and end of life prediction errors of 2.6\% and 1.3\% respectively.

custody_records.raw_content: In this work, a novel acausal and reconfigurable battery pack model is presented. The model structure adopted for the battery cell is based on an equivalent circuit representation. The circuit elements are modified to take account of both hysteresis and diffusion limitation. The latter is known to be a nonlinear function of large operating currents or long operating times. It is shown that the integration of a current dependent time constant within the cell model better emulates the solid diffusional dynamics of lithium intercalation into the active material under large electrical loads. The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified. The cell and scaled-up pack model are parameterized for a number of commercially available cell formats, energy capacities and chemistries. The new models are validated using transient, real-world, electrical data measured from an electric vehicle (EV) operating within an urban environment

custody_records.raw_content: Lithium ion batteries undergo complex electrochemical and mechanical degradation. This complexity is pronounced in applications such as electric vehicles where highly demanding cycles of operation and varying environmental conditions lead to non-trivial interactions of ageing stress factors. This work presents the framework for an ageing diagnostic tool based on identifying the physical parameters of a fundamental electrochemistry-based battery model from non-invasive voltage/current cycling tests. Exploiting the embedded symbolic manipulation tool and global optimiser in MapleSim, computational cost is reduced, significantly facilitating rapid optimisation. The diagnostic tool is used to study the degradation of a 3Ah LiC6/LiNiCoAlO2 battery stored at 45°C at 50% State of Charge for 202 days; the results agree with expected battery degradation

value.mechanism: Capacity fade under heavy load is driven by per-cell current density and temperature: high current density raises overpotential, causing resistive (I²R) heating and lithium plating / SEI growth side reactions whose rates accelerate with temperature (Arrhenius); fade is therefore a function of the thermal-electrochemical stress per cell, not of pack-level nominal capacity. Paralleling N cell banks under an active balancing controller reduces current per bank toward 1/N of the load (governed by Kirchhoff's current law, with impedance-dependent sharing that the controller corrects), which lowers per-cell heating and side-reaction rate; this is a physical current-division effect, not an averaging or "pooling increases power" effect.
value.intervention: Rebuild the pack as a modular multi-bank array of N parallel cell modules, each with its own cell-level fuse, per-bank current-sense shunt, and a balancing controller that continuously trims per-bank current share to keep impedance-driven imbalance within tolerance; add a supercapacitor buffer at the output port to supply load-onset current spikes so the cells never see the transient peak. Thermal design ties per-bank temperature sensing to a current limit that throttles any bank exceeding a set cell temperature.

doi:10.1111/rda.14634.abstract: The impact of beta-carotene on cattle fertility has been investigated in various studies; however, consensus on this issue has not been reached. In the present study, we systematically reviewed and meta-analysed 29 publications conducted between 1984 and 2022, focusing on seven fertility measures, clinical mastitis and milk yield in cows. We did not find statistically significant results in 8 out of 11 parameters (p > .05). Statistically significant results were observed for milk yield (MD: 216.25 kg in 305 days, p = .01, CI: 50.73-381.77), pregnancy at first service (OR: 1.38 CI: 1.08-1.76, p = .01) and clinical mastitis (OR: 0.59, CI: 0.44-0.80, p = .006) in favour of beta-carotene supplementation. The meta-regression revealed significant effects of 'plasma beta-carotene levels' on 'service to per pregnancy' and dose on 'milk yield' (p = .04 and p = 0). In binary outcomes, 'dose × day' and 'plasma beta-carotene concentration in the control group' positively influenced pregnancy at first service (p = .02 and .03). In conclusion, given the positive point direction observed for some variables and insignificant results for others, there is a need for more studies. We note the very high heterogeneity of outcomes and suggest caution in interpreting results.

doi:10.48550/arxiv.2101.04440.title: Automated feature extraction and selection for data-driven models of rapid battery capacity fade and end of life
doi:10.48550/arxiv.2101.04440.abstract: Lithium-ion cells may experience rapid degradation in later life, especially with more extreme usage protocols. The onset of rapid degradation is called the `knee point', and forecasting it is important for the safe and economically viable use for batteries. We propose a data-driven method that uses automated feature selection to produce inputs for a Gaussian process regression model that estimates changes in battery health, from which the entire capacity fade trajectory, knee point and end of life may be predicted. The feature selection procedure flexibly adapts to varying inputs and prioritises those that impact degradation. For the datasets considered, it was found that calendar time and time spent in specific voltage regions had a strong impact on degradation rate. The approach produced median root mean square errors on capacity estimates under 1\%, and also produced median knee point and end of life prediction errors of 2.6\% and 1.3\% respectively.

doi:10.3390/en7095675.title: An Acausal Li-Ion Battery Pack Model for  Automotive Applications
doi:10.3390/en7095675.abstract: In this work, a novel acausal and reconfigurable battery pack model is presented. The model structure adopted for the battery cell is based on an equivalent circuit representation. The circuit elements are modified to take account of both hysteresis and diffusion limitation. The latter is known to be a nonlinear function of large operating currents or long operating times. It is shown that the integration of a current dependent time constant within the cell model better emulates the solid diffusional dynamics of lithium intercalation into the active material under large electrical loads. The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified. The cell and scaled-up pack model are parameterized for a number of commercially available cell formats, energy capacities and chemistries. The new models are validated using transient, real-world, electrical data measured from an electric vehicle (EV) operating within an urban environment

doi:10.1109/vppc.2014.7007040.abstract:
an electric vehicle battery pack may employ cells 

connected electrically in parallel to meet energy and power 

requirements. For the battery management system, cells 

connected in parallel are often treated as a single larger 

component. However, research has identified that the state of 

charge and cell current may not be equal due to differences in 

capacity, impedance and cell temperature. In this paper, the 

authors develop a parallel cell model validated against 

experimental data. The model is used to evaluate cell energy 

variation and the impact this can have on the design of highly 

parallelized battery systems

title:f015376fa8aebfc8.title: Characterising Li-ion battery degradation through the identification of perturbations in electrochemical battery models
title:f015376fa8aebfc8.abstract: Lithium ion batteries undergo complex electrochemical and mechanical degradation. This complexity is pronounced in applications such as electric vehicles where highly demanding cycles of operation and varying environmental conditions lead to non-trivial interactions of ageing stress factors. This work presents the framework for an ageing diagnostic tool based on identifying the physical parameters of a fundamental electrochemistry-based battery model from non-invasive voltage/current cycling tests. Exploiting the embedded symbolic manipulation tool and global optimiser in MapleSim, computational cost is reduced, significantly facilitating rapid optimisation. The diagnostic tool is used to study the degradation of a 3Ah LiC6/LiNiCoAlO2 battery stored at 45°C at 50% State of Charge for 202 days; the results agree with expected battery degradation

design_inputs.input: Mechanism driver (proposed)
design_inputs.value: Capacity fade under heavy load is driven by per-cell current density and temperature: high current density raises overpotential, causing resistive (I²R) heating and lithium plating / SEI growth side reactions whose rates accelerate with temperature (Arrhenius); fade is therefore a function of the thermal-electrochemical stress per cell, not of pack-level nominal capacity. Paralleling N cell banks under an active balancing controller reduces current per bank toward 1/N of the load (governed by Kirchhoff's current law, with impedance-dependent sharing that the controller corrects), which lowers per-cell heating and side-reaction rate; this is a physical current-division effect, not an averaging or "pooling increases power" effect.

proposed_design.input: battery must sustain heavy-load operation for a full work shift without pack swapping.
proposed_design.mechanism: Capacity fade under heavy load is driven by per-cell current density and temperature: high current density raises overpotential, causing resistive (I²R) heating and lithium plating / SEI growth side reactions whose rates accelerate with temperature (Arrhenius); fade is therefore a function of the thermal-electrochemical stress per cell, not of pack-level nominal capacity. Paralleling N cell banks under an active balancing controller reduces current per bank toward 1/N of the load (governed by Kirchhoff's current law, with impedance-dependent sharing that the controller corrects), which lowers per-cell heating and side-reaction rate; this is a physical current-division effect, not an averaging or "pooling increases power" effect.
proposed_design.component_architecture: heat source characterization; conduction path / spreader; reject interface; safety limit interlock

The model structure adopted for the battery cell is based on an equivalent circuit representation. The circuit elements are modified to take account of both hysteresis and diffusion limitation. The latter is known to be a nonlinear function of large operating currents or long operating times. It is shown that the integration of a current dependent time constant within the cell model better emulates the solid diffusional dynamics of lithium intercalation into the active material under large electrical loads. The advantages of an acausal modeling approach, when scaling-up individual cell models into a complete battery system are also presented. Particular consideration is given to emulating the impact of cell to cell variations on pack performance. Using statistical analysis of battery tests, cell model parameter variations are characterized and quantified.
